text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Tax hikes likely after Finance Committee approves cutdown version of government budget.
- Panel recommends raising the cost of foreign workers to employers in Israel.
- United Mizrahi Bank's Victor Medina gets 20 million shekel loan for share purchase.
- High Court ruling paves way for airports authority to divert Ayalon River to make room for a new terminal at Ben-Gurion Airport.
- Tecnomatix Technologies Ltd signs $10 million deal to sell Mazda Motor Corp its computer-aided production engineering products.
- Government budget on Internet starting today. Site is http://www.mof.gov.il.
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross fails to move Hebron talks.
- Firebombs fly in Hebron. Bomb explodes in Alon Shvut.
GLOBES
- Manufacturers' chief Dan Propper wants an 8 percent devaluation, if the interest rate isn't brought down by 2 to 3 percent.
- Map of tourist grant preferences will hit at Eilat and Haifa.
- Israel Electric Co paid an illegel supplement for about 3-1/2 years into the salaries of 16 officials.
HAARETZ
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu conditions further West Bank redeployment on implementation of Palestinian commitments. Ross could return with "new ideas" next week.
- In coming days Housing Ministry will publish tender to market land for 96 homes in Golan Heights town of Katzrin.
MAARIV
- Ross proposes package deal on Hebron.
- The budget: net salaries to be reduced, cigarettes to be more expensive, gasoline price to go up. Salaries to be eroded by 400 shekels a month under new tax arrangements.

- Netanyahu: I expect the cut will bring about a cut in interest rates and a devaluation. Meridor says it's a great accomplishment to cut deficit by seven million shekels, insists it was done without taxes.
- Israeli air force to buy spare parts -- on the Internet.
- Jerusalem police chief warns building of Ras al-Amud Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem could cause serious disturbances.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Treasury considers raising cigarette and petrol prices today.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says war is not in Egyptian lexicon.
- Ross in bid to arrange meeting of Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
- Expectation Bank of Israel will either keep the interest rate where it is or else lower it by a mere 0.3 to 0.5 percent.
- From tomorrow everyone can find Israel's parliament on the Internet at http://www.knesset.gov.il.
